notes: Structural pack only. Entry expectations for CRA roles are set by employers and sponsors rather than by a statutory register, and they vary between organisations. Nothing here is presented as a mandatory requirement: the 'required' list is deliberately empty until a verified requirements review has been completed against current official and employer sources.

usuallyExpected.title: Recognised Good Clinical Practice training
usuallyExpected.detail: Sponsors and contract research organisations commonly expect current ICH GCP training before a monitor works on a study. Which course is accepted varies by employer.

usuallyExpected.title: Working knowledge of the clinical trial lifecycle
usuallyExpected.detail: Protocol and feasibility, site selection and initiation, consent processes, source data verification, deviations, and close-out.

usuallyExpected.title: Life science, nursing or healthcare background
usuallyExpected.detail: Most entrants hold a relevant degree or a clinical registration. Employers also recruit from research delivery and laboratory roles.

careerEnhancing.title: Experience on the site side of a study
careerEnhancing.detail: Time as a research nurse, trial coordinator or clinical trial administrator is well regarded, because it shows how a protocol actually behaves in a clinic.

careerEnhancing.title: Depth in a therapy area
careerEnhancing.detail: Oncology, rare disease and advanced therapies are frequently recruited for and reward specific clinical understanding.

careerEnhancing.title: Audit, quality or inspection experience
careerEnhancing.detail: Source data verification and deviation handling are quality activities, so prior audit experience transfers directly.

optional.title: Postgraduate qualification in clinical research
optional.detail: Helpful for career changers who need to evidence the subject matter, but not a general expectation for entry.

optional.title: Willingness to travel to investigator sites
optional.detail: Site monitoring has traditionally been a travelling role, though remote and hybrid monitoring models have grown. This is a working-pattern consideration rather than something to develop, so it sits here rather than among the expectations.

milestones.title: Complete recognised GCP training
milestones.meaning: A current ICH GCP certificate from a course your target employers accept.
milestones.why: It is the common denominator across sponsor and CRO job descriptions, and usually the cheapest gap to close first.
milestones.action: Complete a recognised GCP course and keep the certificate current.

milestones.title: Learn the trial lifecycle end to end
milestones.meaning: Being able to describe what happens from feasibility to close-out, and who is accountable at each step.
milestones.why: Monitoring decisions only make sense in the context of the whole study.
milestones.action: Work through a study from protocol to close-out, or shadow a monitoring visit if your organisation runs studies.

milestones.title: Build documented research or quality evidence
milestones.meaning: Concrete examples: consent processes, data queries, deviations, audits, or coordinating a study visit.
milestones.why: Employers recruit on demonstrated activity, not on training certificates alone.
milestones.action: Volunteer for study delivery, data review or audit work, and record what you did.

milestones.title: Bridge role, or a first monitoring role
milestones.meaning: A clinical trial administrator, coordinator, in-house CRA or research delivery post.
milestones.why: Most people reach CRA through one of these rather than directly.
milestones.action: Target bridge roles in parallel with CRA applications.

milestones.title: Clinical Research Associate
milestones.meaning: Monitoring assigned investigator sites against the protocol and GCP.
milestones.action: Apply once GCP training and demonstrable research evidence are in place.

milestones.title: Senior CRA, then trial management
milestones.meaning: Larger or more complex studies, mentoring monitors, then owning study delivery.
milestones.why: Shows where the route leads after entry.
milestones.action: Plan for it, but do not treat it as a step to take now.

entryRoutes: Research delivery or site-based study coordination, then monitoring
Clinical trial administrator or in-house CRA within a CRO, then field monitoring
Clinical or laboratory background plus GCP training and a therapy-area fit
bridgeRoles: Research Nurse or Clinical Research Practitioner
